purpose: Test the tempting next compression of the smooth-C4 Hamiltonian carrier: decompose each proper inner C4 colouring into one of three S3-orbits tau and one gauge g in S3, then eliminate the gauges independently on every pair of C4 components. Give a twelve-vertex smooth 4-regular Hamiltonian graph for which this pairwise orbit projection accepts a tau assignment although no globally consistent gauges exist. The lost datum is an S3 holonomy/cocycle consistency condition around the component interaction cycle.

external_source_control.fact: Fleischner--Sabidussi prove NP-completeness of 3-colourability for smooth 4-regular Hamiltonian graphs whose complementary inner cycles have constant length at least four. Smooth means that the cyclic order of vertices of each inner cycle agrees with their cyclic order on the supplied Hamiltonian cycle.
external_source_control.reference: H. Fleischner and G. Sabidussi, 3-colorability of 4-regular hamiltonian graphs, Journal of Graph Theory 42(2) (2003), 125-140, DOI 10.1002/jgt.10079.

finite_control.interpretation: Positions 0,...,11 occur in this order on the Hamiltonian C12. The symbol at a position names its complementary C4 component. For each symbol x, connect its four occurrences cyclically in their Hamiltonian occurrence order.
structural_checks: Every symbol appears exactly four times and equal symbols are never adjacent on the cyclic Hamiltonian word, so H and the complementary 2-factor are edge-disjoint.
The resulting graph is simple and every vertex has two H-neighbours plus two inner-C4 neighbours, hence degree four.
Each inner C4 is smooth by construction because its occurrence order is exactly its cycle order.
Exhaustive evaluation of all 3^12 vertex-colour assignments finds zero proper 3-colourings.

C4_orbit_coordinates.decomposition: Every proper 3-colouring of a labelled C4 is uniquely g(rep_tau) for tau in {0,1,2} and g in S3. Each orbit has six colourings and the three orbits partition all 18 proper C4 colourings.
C4_orbit_coordinates.pair_projection: For two C4 components a,b, collect all Hamiltonian edges between their occurrence ports. Define R_ab to contain (tau_a,tau_b) iff there exist gauges g_a,g_b in S3 satisfying every such cross-edge NEQ constraint. This existential quantification is performed independently for each component pair.

Hamiltonian_port_bundles.note: A port pair [p,q] means that the p-th occurrence of the lower-numbered component and q-th occurrence of the higher-numbered component are consecutive on H.

exact_pairwise_orbit_relations.pairwise_check: (1,1) is in R01, (1,0) is in R12, and (1,0) is in R02. Therefore the orbit-only pairwise projected CSP accepts tau=(1,1,0).

holonomy_contradiction.setup: Let component 0 use tau1 with colour names A=(a0,a1,a2), component 1 use tau1 with B=(b0,b1,b2), and component 2 use tau0 with alternating colours C=(c0,c1), with c2 the third colour.
holonomy_contradiction.from_R02_bundle: The four 0--2 inequalities force a0 to differ from both c0 and c1, hence a0=c2; the remaining inequalities then force a1=c0 and a2=c1.
holonomy_contradiction.from_R12_bundle: The four 1--2 inequalities force b0 to differ from both c0 and c1, hence b0=c2; the remaining inequalities force b1=c1 and b2=c0.
holonomy_contradiction.closing_edge: The 0--1 bundle contains port edge (0,0), which requires a0!=b0. But the two independently forced gauges give a0=b0=c2. Contradiction.
holonomy_contradiction.conclusion: There is no global triple (g0,g1,g2) in S3^3 realizing tau=(1,1,0), despite every pair projection accepting its local tau pair. Exhaustive evaluation of all 6^3 gauge triples independently confirms the contradiction.

main_theorem.name: PAIRWISE_EXISTENTIAL_S3_GAUGE_ELIMINATION_IS_NOT_EXACT
main_theorem.statement: For the smooth-C4 Hamiltonian carrier, replacing each pair of interacting C4 components by the existentially gauge-projected binary relation R_ab on the three orbit labels tau can introduce spurious globally feasible orbit assignments. Pairwise projection does not preserve the global colouring relation.
main_theorem.reason: The witnesses used by different pair projections may require incompatible gauges for the same component. Global gauges are potentials on the component interaction graph; their relative S3 transformations must satisfy cycle/holonomy consistency, which independent pair projection discards.

killed: Eliminate each C4 S3 gauge independently per neighbouring component pair and solve only the resulting 3-state pairwise orbit CSP.
Treat existence of a relative-gauge witness on every interaction edge as sufficient for existence of global component gauges.
Any contraction that forgets cycle consistency among relative S3 gauges while claiming exactness on the smooth-C4 carrier.
positive: The missing information is sharply localized: retain either one S3 gauge per component or relative S3 gain sets together with global cycle consistency.
The explicit twelve-vertex control is small enough for exhaustive replay and should be mandatory for every future orbit/interlacement contraction.
A spanning-tree gauge fixing is exact for functional relative-gain edges; only non-singleton gain sets create branching/constraint propagation. This gives a concrete next reduction target.
firewall: This is a barrier to one compression strategy, not a lower bound against all polynomial algorithms.
It does not prove that S3-gain consistency with set-valued edge constraints is hard in every restricted source class.

next_target.name: E8_S3_GAIN_SET_RIGID_EDGE_CONTRACTION_AND_HOLONOMY_KERNEL_V7_2
next_target.directive: Keep the three C4 orbit labels but do not existentially forget gauges pairwise. For each interaction bundle and orbit pair compute the allowed relative-gain set S_ij subseteq S3. Contract every connected region whose gain constraints become functional singletons after propagation, using a spanning-tree gauge and exact cycle-product checks. Characterize the residual non-singleton gain-set atoms and test whether they admit polynomial closure or reproduce a hard finite-domain CSP. Mandatory controls: the v7.1 twelve-vertex holonomy graph, the v6.8 mutation pair, K5, and the fixed-inner-cycle smooth Hamiltonian NP-hard source. No enumeration over 6^k gauges is permitted.
